citation_info.title: Centralizing the Student Lens: Design and Evaluation of a Learning Analytics Dashboard for Academic Advising in Higher Education

document_type.es: Artículo aceptado en el World Engineering Education Forum, WEEF (IFEES & GEDC) 2026, Cartagena de Indias, Colombia, 22-25 de septiembre de 2026
document_type.en: Paper accepted at the World Engineering Education Forum, WEEF (IFEES & GEDC) 2026, Cartagena de Indias, Colombia, September 22-25, 2026

abstract.en: This paper presents SASP (Socioeconomic and Academic Student Profile), an institution-wide learning analytics dashboard developed and deployed at Universidad de los Andes (Colombia) — embedded within *No estás solx*, the university's existing student support platform — designed to improve the quality of academic advising in engineering education. SASP addresses a persistent challenge in higher education: student information relevant to advising is often fragmented across multiple institutional systems, limiting timely, consistent, and evidence-based support. SASP was created through a year-long iterative co-design process with the Vice Dean's Office for Student Affairs in the School of Engineering and integrates academic performance, course history, socioeconomic context, scheduling, and institutional support records into a single interface. The dashboard embodies four design principles: (1) multi-dimensional centralization; (2) per-academic-level context switching; (3) subject-area filtering as a cross-cutting analytical lens; and (4) embedding within an existing, trusted portal. To evaluate its contribution, we gathered survey data from 117 academic advisors and nine months of behavioral telemetry. Results show strong institutional adoption (94.9% of respondents had used SASP; 72.7% were returning users) and positive perceptions of its value for advising. Data centralization was the highest-rated feature, 91% of respondents who used SASP during counseling sessions found it useful, and advisors reported that the dashboard improved access to relevant information, facilitated understanding of students' academic trajectories, and supported the identification of at-risk cases. Advisors also rated SASP as sufficiently complete to serve as the primary tool during a counseling session. These findings suggest that integrated learning analytics tools can strengthen the quality, consistency, and timeliness of academic support in engineering education when they are embedded into real institutional workflows. Beyond the specific system, this study contributes empirically grounded design principles for scalable advising infrastructures in higher education.

citation_info.title: MeSHClass-ES and AnatEM-ES: Open Resources for Spanish Biomedical NLP

document_type.es: Artículo presentado en BioNLP 2026 (Biomedical Natural Language Processing Workshop, ACL), San Diego, California, pp. 617-629
document_type.en: Paper presented at BioNLP 2026 (Biomedical Natural Language Processing Workshop, ACL), San Diego, California, pp. 617-629

abstract.en: Despite Spanish being one of the most widely spoken languages in the world, biomedical NLP resources and systematic evaluations remain limited relative to English. We address this gap by constructing and releasing two Spanish biomedical corpora: (1) MeSHClass-ES, a 29,063 abstract bilingual corpus translated from PubMed with Opus-MT, and (2) AnatEM-ES, the AnatEM anatomical entity corpus translated with a chunk-level LLM-based pipeline that jointly preserves BIO annotations across 13,849 entity mentions. Both corpora achieve a mean COMET score of 0.73 despite using different translation systems. We benchmark nine encoder models spanning general-domain Spanish, domain-specific, and multilingual architectures for both tasks. RigoBERTa-2.0 leads both tasks (micro-F1 classification 0.69, tied with SciBETO-large; NER F1 0.66). Both domain pretraining and model capacity drive performance, with the gap slightly more pronounced for NER (4-point spread) than classification (3-point spread). XLM-RoBERTa-large emerges as a competitive multilingual baseline. A parallel evaluation of four open-weight decoders (7-9B) reveals a task-dependent encoder-decoder gap: QLoRA-adapted Gemma-2-9B reaches 88% of the best encoder on classification (micro-F1 .61 vs .69), but for NER every decoder configuration we tested stays at or below 40% of the best encoder F1. We release both corpora on the HuggingFace Hub, translation pipelines, and evaluation code on GitHub.

citation_info.title: Classification of Chest XRay Diseases through image processing and analysis techniques

abstract.en: Multi-Classification Chest X-Ray Images are one of the most prevalent forms of radiological examination used for diagnosing thoracic diseases. In this study, we offer a concise overview of several methods employed for tackling this task, including DenseNet121. In addition, we deploy an open-source web-based application. In our study, we conduct tests to compare different methods and see how well they work. We also look closely at the weaknesses of the methods we propose and suggest ideas for making them better in the future. Our code is available at: https://github.com/AML4206-MINE20242/Proyecto_AML

citation_info.title: Efficient Multilingual Dialogue Processing via Translation Pipelines and Distilled Language Models

abstract.en: This paper presents team Kl33n3x's multilingual dialogue summarization and question answering system developed for the NLPAI4Health 2025 shared task. The approach employs a three-stage pipeline: forward translation from Indic languages to English, multitask text generation using a 2.55B parameter distilled language model, and reverse translation back to source languages. By leveraging knowledge distillation techniques, this work demonstrates that compact models can achieve highly competitive performance across nine languages. The system achieved strong win rates across the competition's tasks, with particularly robust performance on Marathi (86.7% QnA), Tamil (86.7% QnA), and Hindi (80.0% QnA), demonstrating the effectiveness of translation-based approaches for low-resource language processing without task-specific fine-tuning.
